comments:
Although I wouldn't call software development my absolute strongest skill just yet, I still have valuable experience in the area through my extracurriculars:

- I'm a part of UTD's multidisciplinary SWE Match program. My group's project is called PAIGE, a small handheld personal AI assistant that helps you maintain productivity, reduce screen time, and manage stress almost entirely through voice commands. I'm part of my group's software track and am actively learning Python libraries like PyAudio and AWS services like Amazon S3. In the near future, I'll be learning Boto3 to call AWS APIs with Python for speech-to-text transcription so that PAIGE can parse your commands. Working with my teammates in hardware and research has also helped introduce me to other fields such as computer engineering and biomedical engineering, which have made my skillset more versatile. BrainCharge's Caregiver Compassion Bot reminded me of PAIGE, especially since both are multidisciplinary and involve machine learning; Thus, I'm confident I'd be a great fit for the Caregiver Compassion Bot!

- At HackUTD 2025, my group's project, UpGuardian, won 3rd place for State Farm's track and honorable mention for Nvidia through its utilization of Nvidia's Nemotron. Working on UpGuardian helped introduce me to agentic AI and how it could be implemented into software. Agentic AI builds on machine learning, so I plunged straight into learning foundational machine learning concepts by helping implement Nemotron. Machine learning is a fundamental part of the Caregiver Compassion Bot, and I'm ready to apply my experiences from UpGuardian to the Caregiver Compassion Bot. 

Wherever I'm placed, I'm excited to uplift others with my current strengths while learning new skills from my classmates in EPICS! Thank you for reading, and I'll see you soon!
